newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. envoy fails again to clinch Hebron deal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy fails again to clinch Hebron deal.

text.p: A U.S. peace mediator failed to clinch a deal on a troop pullout from the West Bank town of Hebron in talks with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.
Envoy Dennis Ross met Arafat for two hours on Saturday and later held talks for almost three hours with Netanyahu on implementing the long overdue Israeli army redeployment.
He also saw the two leaders on Friday.

"There are still a few details in the agreement which must be worked on," Netanyahu's office said, without elaborating, in a statement after the late-night talks on Saturday at the prime minister's residence.
"Ross will continue with his contacts between the sides. At this stage, no meeting has been set between Netanyahu and Arafat," the statement said.
Earlier in self-ruled Gaza, Ross declined to disclose the sticking points still delaying a Hebron deal, which had appeared to be close to being signed over the last two weeks.
"We're close but you know you have to resolve everything to have an agreement," Ross said.

Palestinian cabinet minister Nabil Shaath has said the central issue blocking an accord was Israel's refusal to commit itself to a timetable for further West Bank pullbacks after Hebron, as stipulated in previous peace deals.

Israel was to have redeployed its troops in Hebron some 10 months ago under a 1995 interim agreement but violence and security concerns have held it up. Some 400 Jews live or study in the town, home to more than 100,000 Palestinians.
Netanyahu's right-wing government has also missed a September deadline for the first of three pullbacks from rural areas of the West Bank.

Israeli Tourism Minister Moshe Katzav said such land handovers -- agreed by the previous Labour-led government -- would weaken Israel's negotiating position in future talks with the PLO on a permanent peace settlement.
"It is inconceivable that we should give up strategic assets before permanent status negotiations are completed," Katzav told Israel's Channel One Television.
If Ross fails in his current mediation mission, the U.S. could choose to shift its diplomatic efforts to home ground.

Both Netanyahu and Arafat have invitations from U.S. President Bill Clinton to visit Washington separately early this year, although no precise dates have been set, spokesmen for the Israeli and Palestinian leaders said.
Against the backdrop of the Hebron issue, Jewish settlers were due to remove seven mobile homes from a West Bank hilltop on Sunday under a deal reached with government officials.
Their bid on Friday to set up a new outpost near the settlement of Beit El, north of the Palestinian town of Ramallah, drew sharp PLO condemnation.
The settlers said they had struck a deal with the government under which they would remove the caravans in exchange for a meeting to discuss expanding Beit El.
Settler leaders said they expected to hold talks on Sunday with Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai.
